denominator_sound_comparison.statement: Restricted to ratios whose denominator interval excludes zero -- the only ones this paper's own Section 5.3 standard permits quoting, and using the fold-matched-carveout-corrected severities this paper currently reports as numerators (+0.0060, +0.0159; not the superseded shipped +0.0093, +0.0250) -- the mechanism-and-harness axis (9.2-24.3x) is AT LEAST COMPARABLE TO, AND PLAUSIBLY LARGER THAN, the operating-point axis (2.2-14.3x). It is NOT asserted to be strictly the largest of the three: its own lower end (9.2x) sits below the operating-point axis's upper end (14.3x), so the two ranges overlap substantially. Candidate count remains the smallest on every convention.

verdict.statement: AS RAW SPANS: operating point 48.6-68.3x within this harness; mechanism-and-harness up to 38.3x across harnesses at a matched operating point; candidate count 1.6-7.1x within an operating point (1.1-1.4x excluding the low-contrast K=15 column). The first two are the same order of magnitude and the third is roughly an order weaker -- but the first and third use denominators whose intervals include zero. RESTRICTED TO SOUND DENOMINATORS, which is the only comparison this paper's own Section 5.3 standard permits: operating point 2.2-14.3x, mechanism-and-harness 9.2-24.3x, candidate count 1.8-4.2x -- and the mechanism-and-harness axis is AT LEAST COMPARABLE TO, AND PLAUSIBLY LARGER THAN, the operating-point axis (not asserted as strictly the largest of the three: their sound ranges overlap). On either reading the paper's former claim that severity is governed by candidate count and operating point RATHER THAN mechanism is not merely unproven; these numbers point the other way. It is withdrawn from the title and abstract. NOTE: the RAW-SPAN mechanism-and-harness figure above (38.3x) is sourced from operating_point_transport_check.json's own gap_spread_ratio and, like the probit-interpolated and arm-matched sensitivity figures, has not been re-derived from the corrected fold-matched-carveout severities in this round; only the denominator-sound with_intervals figures above use the corrected numerators.
verdict.precision_caveat: The operating-point and candidate-count full-range spans quoted above use denominators whose intervals include zero and therefore have no finite upper confidence limit. See denominator_sound_comparison for the version that meets this paper's own Section 5.3 standard.
